Hello Graham,

I appreciate your follow-up. Thank you!

The problem with using the draw button to plot the tree persists regardless of whether I load a .rattle projects or load in a data set from .RData.

I got a bit further in your book and learned about conditional trees. I tried that and the draw button worked fine!

Below is the detailed transcript.

By the way, I read up on rpart and party packages as your book suggests and have a question about using "poisson" option (either in Rattle or in R in general). This is not covered in your book, but maybe you can tell me  whether I am on the right track or not.  I have a data set where the target variable is a number of times a certain question on a survey received a "yes" answer. The surveys pertain to events that may be attended by one person or multiple people. Sometimes we get only 1 survey per event. Sometimes several different people who participated in the same event fill out surveys (one survey per person). I want to use the number of "yes" answers that  an event received as a target variable and use a bunch of other variables (some categorical and some numerical) as predictors. Clearly, the number of yes votes depends on how many surveys we have filled out for that event (in addition to potentially depending on other predictors, such as where it was held, what kind of event, etc.) because id we had only 1 survey, then we can only get a maximum of 1 yes answer, while if we got 3 surveys for an event we can get up to 3 yes votes. I get an impression that I should use "poisson" model in rpart and make "y variable" be a 2 column variable with 1 column being the number of "yes" votes we got  for a given individual event and the other column being the number of surveys filled out for that event. I get an impression that I do not have that option in the ctree package (so I cannot use the nice plot that the draw button produces for the conditional tree). Does this seem right?

Many thanks!

Hi Graham,

I did some troubleshooting and got rattle to work on Mountain Lion!

I also found some interesting things and a possible rattle bug as well...

Interesting Point #1
The AT&T website no longer hosts the GTK 2.18.5 framework (which is at a URL that rattle looks for during rattle installation).  The file is now at this URL:
http://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/R/GTK_2.18.5-X11.pkg

Interesting Point #2
Apple's new "Mountain Lion" OS does not include X11 (XQuartz) and the XQuartz application will need to be downloaded and installed in order for rattle to work properly.  It can be downloaded at:
http://xquartz.macosforge.org/landing/

messages.body_plain:
Hi Barbara,

I don't think the install.packages() function will work in this case because a PKG file is a Mac Application package file (not an R Package file).

I would install the GTK PKG file without using R at all.  Just install it by clicking it in your Downloads Folder.

Shutdown R and click the link below to download it:

http://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/R/GTK_2.18.5-X11.pkg

Then, go into your Downloads folder and install the PKG file by clicking it.  Mountain Lion may say something like "unable to install because this is not from a known vendor...".  This feature is called "GateKeeper" in Mountain Lion and prevents viruses, etc...

If you get this GateKeeper message, you can bypass GateKeeper it by "control-clicking" on the PKG file (inside your Downloads folder).  Here is more info on GateKeeper:

http://support.apple.com/kb/HT5290

- Ray
